issues.description: Method PersonService.savePerson has conflicting access modifiers across artifacts. In the template (template_repository/src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/PersonService.java) the method is declared public: "public Person savePerson(Person person)". In the solution (solution_repository/src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/PersonService.java) the same method is declared private: "private Person savePerson(Person person)". However the solution's REST controller (solution_repository/src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java) calls personService.savePerson(...) from a different package, which would not be able to access a private method. This discrepancy would cause a compilation error or confuse students about the intended service API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility of PersonService.savePerson consistent and accessible to the REST resource. Preferred fix: change the declaration in solution_repository/src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/PersonService.java from private to public (public Person savePerson(Person person)) so PersonResource can call it. Alternatively, if the intent is to keep the service method non-public, modify PersonResource to call a public service method that performs the same save/update behavior. Ensure the service API matches the problem statement's intended usage and the REST resource calls.
